findings.description: `host.endswith(domain)` has no dot boundary. With partner domain `shop.example`, the origin `https://evilshop.example` or `https://attackershop.example` passes. The policy then reflects that origin with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, so any attacker who registers a domain that merely ends with the partner string can make credentialed cross-origin calls. Those calls can read a member's balance and redeem rewards using the member's session cookie.
findings.suggestion: Require an exact match or a subdomain match: `host == domain or host.endswith('.' + domain)`.
findings.title: Partner domain check uses bare endswith, allowing attacker-controlled lookalike domains

findings.description: For partner-domain matching, `parts.hostname` drops the port and userinfo. An origin such as `https://user@shop.example:8443` is treated as allowed, and the raw header is then reflected back. The path and query check does not cover these components. Origins with arbitrary ports on a partner host are accepted, which is broader than intended.
findings.suggestion: Compare `parts.netloc` against the hostname, or reject origins where `parts.port`, `parts.username` or `parts.password` is set.
findings.title: Port and userinfo in origin not constrained for partner match
